problem: Prior continuous VLN (VLN-CE) agents rely on either local grid-style reasoning or a topological graph alone, so they lack a combination of short-term local and long-term global spatial memory.
motivation: Navigation in free 3D continuous space needs both fine-grained local obstacle and layout reasoning and long-range planning over visited places. Map representations that suit each horizon could improve success rate, but only the abstract is available, so details are limited.
key_idea: Build grid maps for short-term reasoning and topological maps for long-term reasoning, then fuse their navigation scores through hybrid action fusion to choose the final action.
insight: According to the abstract, ablations show that adding map representations improves navigation success rate, and three pretraining tasks help the model understand multimodal information and use map information. No further specifics are available from the abstract alone.
method: Grid map: built from continuous observations and used for short-term (local) reasoning.
Topological map: built from acquired information and used for long-term (global) reasoning.
Hybrid action fusion: combines navigation scores from the grid and topological maps with an algorithm to determine the final action space.
Pretraining: three pretraining tasks improve multimodal understanding and map utilization.

setting.action_space: continuous-environment actions derived from fused grid/topological scores (details not given)
